findings.text: Futex wait entry rejects out of mask extended flags, normalizes to internal flags, validates both value operands, optionally arms a high resolution timeout for the requested clock, calls the core wait, then releases timeout state and returns the core result.

Requeue entry rejects any flags and empty waiter input, parses exactly two futex descriptors for wake marking, mandates identical normalized flags on both, takes the compare value from the first, and delegates to core requeue with wake and requeue counts.

Compatibility robust list set enforces exact header size and stores the user pointer in current task futex state; get resolves the target list with error propagation, then reports the header size and converted pointer to user, failing on user memory errors.

32-bit time wrapper masks the command, loads an old 32-bit timeout only when the command accepts one, initializes kernel timeout with error propagation, and forwards all operands to the common futex dispatcher.

Wake marking refuses priority inheritance waiters, otherwise removes the waiter from its bucket list and publishes a null lock pointer with release ordering so a concurrently waking task may reclaim the entry without locks.
Marked wake holds a task reference across the unqueue attempt, releases it on refusal, and on success queues the task on a safe wake queue so actual wakeup happens after the bucket lock is dropped.
Interrupted wait restart rebuilds an optional timeout pointer from saved flags, disables further automatic restart, and reissues the wait with saved address, flags, value and bitset.
Non-instrumentable diagnostic reports improper interrupt restore while interrupts are enabled, bracketed to allow instrumentation inside the warning path.
Lock event counters live under a fixed debugfs directory name owned by the lock events module.
Counter files use read-only root access and the reset control uses write-only root access; the reset file has a fixed dot-prefixed name.
Event name table is sized one past the event count to hold the reset entry; the event enum defines the count and aliases the reset identifier to that count.
Per CPU unsigned counters indexed by event identifier hold lock event totals; increment and add helpers operate on the current CPU instance.
Counter read takes the identifier from inode private data, rejects out of range identifiers, sums that counter across all possible CPUs, and returns a decimal line via a bounded helper.

Counter write acts only when addressed to the reset identifier, zeroing every event counter on every CPU with volatile stores; other identifiers leave state unchanged while still reporting full consumption.
Lock event file operations bind the module read and write helpers with the default seek behavior.
One build filters paravirtual spin events on native hosts by caching the host kind once and skipping names with the paravirtual prefix; the alternate build never skips.
Boot initializer creates the debugfs directory and one file per retained event plus the reset file, removes the whole tree and warns on any creation failure.
Counting helpers either conditionally increment or unconditionally add on the current CPU, while the disabled build discards the increment expression without touching state.
Proving and statistics controls exist either as writable integers defaulting to enabled or as constant zero when their build options are absent.
Lock dependency controls are exposed as integer sysctl entries under the kernel table, registered once at boot.

Global validator state is guarded by an architecture spinlock plus an owner pointer and per CPU recursion depth; acquisition and release both require interrupts disabled, track recursion, record and clear the owner, and warn on owner mismatch.

Graph access takes the validator lock, counts the acquisition, and aborts without holding the lock when global checking is already disabled; unlock simply releases it, and one helper disables checking while releasing.

Dependency edges live in a fixed array with a global used count; deferred reclamation uses a list of zapped entries plus a chain bitmap, double buffered behind a read-copy-update head with index and scheduled flag.
Key, class and chain hash tables have power of two sizes derived from configured bit counts, with helpers hashing key addresses and chain values into bucket indices.
Classes and keys are counted globally with high water and zap accounting; per CPU tables hold per class statistics indexed by distance from the class base.
Held lock identity packs class index with a read flag shifted by the key bit width; chain keys evolve by mixing the next index into a split 64-bit accumulator.
Task initialization clears held depth and recursion and installs the initial chain key; a separate setter records the self test task pointer.
Verbose filtering is compiled out in this lane: both verbosity queries return false and the class filter rejects every class.
Saved stack traces carry a hash list node, hash value, entry count and aligned flexible entries; a size macro expresses the header length in words.

Trace saving appends to a static buffer, refuses with validator shutdown and diagnostic when space is exhausted, otherwise captures the current stack, hashes entries, and returns an existing identical trace or links the new one into its hash bucket.
Statistics queries count all saved traces and separately count non-empty hash buckets.
Hard interrupt, soft interrupt and process chain totals plus maximum observed depth are tracked globally; per CPU validator counters live in a dedicated statistics structure.
Usage state names distinguish interrupt contexts and read versus write, covering both used-in and enabled variants.

Statistics aggregation sums contention points and bounce counts across CPUs and merges wait and hold times by keeping extremes and accumulating totals and samples; clearing zeroes per CPU and class totals.
Hold time accounting is skipped when statistics are disabled, otherwise it measures elapsed time since acquisition and attributes it to read or write hold totals; the alternate build does nothing.
An object counts as static when in core data, read-only data, boot init memory while init lives, kernel or module per CPU memory, or module address space.
Class naming reuses the version of a matching key adjusted for subclass, otherwise assigns one past the highest version sharing the same name, or a first version when unnamed or unique.
Key assignment canonicalizes per CPU addresses to their base, accepts other static objects by address, and otherwise shuts down validation with a diagnostic instead of registering transient storage.
List membership is decided by linear pointer comparison over the given head.
Waking a priority inheritance waiter through the non-inheritance path warns and refuses; callers must route such waiters through the inheritance path.
Publishing the null lock pointer must stay ordered after list removal, otherwise a spinner could free the waiter while it still appears queued.
Registering a lock whose key storage is not persistent disables the validator permanently with a diagnostic; callers must annotate or statically allocate keys.
Exhausting the static stack trace store disables validation and emits a sizing diagnostic; the configured maximum must cover the workload.
Restoring interrupts while already enabled triggers a one-time warning path that must not itself be instrumented.
